candidate.title: Nextera Mate Pair
candidate.scope: The single Nextera Mate Pair product/library-preparation outline in the assigned Illumina poster panel: DNA tagmentation with biotinylated junction adapters, circularization, fragmentation, isolation of the junction-bearing fragment, adapter ligation, and denaturation/amplification to a cluster-ready P5/P7 library. The intact and fragmented circles are successive views linked by the Fragment arrow, not alternative workflows. The biological material represented is DNA; the panel does not identify a specimen, size range, protocol version, or sequencing read arrangement. This is a schematic-level architecture supported by the diagram and catalogue title, not a complete experimental protocol.

features: Blue parallel strands depict double-stranded DNA extending beyond the illustrated region; biological source and fragment length are not specified.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Transposase-associated biotinylated junction adapters act on the input duplex. The long DNA becomes linear DNA fragments bearing adapter/biotin marks at their ends. The two successive downward views are retained within this single named transformation; no separate size-selection or cleanup step is drawn.
operations.mechanism: The labeled transposase and adapter complexes mediate the depicted combination of DNA fragmentation and end tagging; transposase is a catalyst, not a sequenced substrate.
operations.information_effect: Creates tagged fragment termini that can subsequently be brought together.
